question.text: Daily mark-to-market (MTM) settlement in derivatives means that:

answer.text: Open positions are valued at the daily settlement price and gains/losses are settled on T+1 basis
All contracts are closed and settled at the end of each trading day
The margin requirement remains constant throughout the contract period
Settlement happens only on the expiry date of the contract

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 206, all derivative contracts are settled on T+1 by computing the difference between the traded price and the daily settlement price. Pages 207-209 support the final settlement and the dynamic margining/risk-management context that surrounds the daily MTM process. The Trap: Contracts are not closed and re-opened daily — positions stay open and are marked to the settlement price. Margins are dynamic, not constant. Settlement only on expiry describes final settlement, not the daily MTM mechanic. Note: Daily MTM keeps unrealised P&L from accumulating; final settlement is a separate event that occurs on the contract's expiry date.
